findings.text: The second partial-move sequence has correct document-capture down/move/up coordinates and pointerId, no drops, yet zero final transform in both modes. The first no-move sequence passes.

Controller pointerdown does not reject Mermaid nodes or edges. It rejects non-left button, ancestor a, annotations panel or annotation controls. Accepted down saves exact event coordinates and current pan; matching up calls movePan before stop.

With accepted down, matching pointerId, no intervening drag cancellation, paused/disposed false and no later fit, final coordinate arithmetic forces pan45/25. The retained document-only recorder cannot establish those premises.

ResizeObserver calls only walkthrough.updateGeometry. That method changes overlay visibility/geometry, not pan/zoom. onPreview calls transform using existing pan; it does not reset pan. The fit function explicitly resets pan and zoom, and is called by Fit and walkthrough overview.

Original harness clicks Fit before each phase and recomputes the same viewport centre. It records only pointerdown/move/up at document capture; no target/currentTarget, cancel, got/lostcapture, buttons, capture state, event timestamps or controller drag state is retained.

Retained final PNG places observed centre near the connector between nodes, with annotation controls at bottom right. Nodes would be allowed anyway. The PNG is captured after failure and cannot prove the pointerdown hit path.

A matching-id lostpointercapture or pointercancel after accepted down would clear drag and allow the observed zero transform. A delayed same-id capture-loss from an earlier gesture is not ruled out by the recorder. No such event is retained; this is not a proven cause.

A rejected or non-viewport down, prepare/pause cancellation, or later explicit Fit could also explain no final pan. Original evidence lacks the event/handler ordering needed to select one. Generic async resize reset is unsupported by this controller code.
